ENGLISH MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ENGLISH MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Extensive Listening ● listening for enjoyment and g.

3. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

4. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

5. When practising Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.

7. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .

8. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goes
   C. goed
   D. going

11. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 9.2.1 Close reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Critical reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Sentence types and subject- verb agreement ● sentences: inversions ● subject-ver and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing: blog posts and newspaper articles 9.4.2 Making writing livel and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 9.2.1 Close reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
